subject: Weighted LDA - a weight for every pair word-topic

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: Weighted LDA - a weight for every pair word-topic
parts:
Hello Community,

I have an LDA-like model with known phi (probability of words in topics). For some topics some words are not indicative and with little data, the noise is detrimental. I want to try to weight words for each topic.

I have read that to weight an observation is enough to do

increment_log_prob(my_prob * WEIGHT);

However in my case I have (for example):

increment_log_prob(   log_sum_exp(    [-5, -3, -2]  *  WEIGHT_array(3)     )     )

I am not sure if this is the proper way to do it.
Thanks a lot.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Weighted LDA - a weight for every pair word-topic
parts:
What's detrimental to what goal?

Weighting destroys the generative nature of the model, which is
usually a very bad idea as it makes the results hard to
interpret and it makes the model hard to generalize or combine
with other models.

The log density only matters up to a constant, so your
entire expression doesn't do anything because there aren't any
pareters in it. Could you say a bit more specifically what
you're going to do?

If you have fixed topic probabilities, then you only need
to estimate the theta for each document (and also the prior,
either a Dirichlet or logistic normal as in the correlated
topic model). For that, you won't get any effect whatsoever
from a word that has the same probability in each topic. So
if you have things that feel like stopwords ("the", "is", etc.),
then what you probably want to do is think about a stronger prior
on them in estimating the phi (topic-word probabilities).

- Bob

What's detrimental to what goal?

usually a very bad idea as it makes the results hard to

The log density only matters up to a constant, so your
entire expression doesn't do anything because there aren't any
pareters in it.  Could you say a bit more specifically what
you're going to do?

I am working in gene expression deconvolution. Where I have ~500 genes (words) with known probability to appear into a cell-type (topic n = 5), gene counts from 0 to 10000, and 20-30 samples (documents). I would like to identify the probability of cell-type in samples (topics in documents). Every of the 5 topic is present in every document.

The problem is that I don't get great results, and I was thinking that just the minority of genes are "markers" of a particular cell type. So if the 499 (limit case) of genes expression values that I provide  as Phi for cell-type X have the same probability (plus a big noise) to all other 4 cell-types (except one for example) , and just 1 gene contains signal (differential presence) that distinguish it from all other 4 cell-types, then putting weight 0 on the 499 should help to drive the likelihood with only the bit of information where the ration signal noise is likely to be higher.

If you have fixed topic probabilities, then you only need
to estimate the theta for each document (and also the prior,
either a Dirichlet or logistic normal as in the correlated
topic model)
The theta prior is given and is hyperparametrized with array(n) <- 1 (I was also thinking to have hyperparameters predicted)

For that, you won't get any effect whatsoever
from a word that has the same probability in each topic.

My fear is that although the probability is the same, the noise (on the word probability in the topic in the mix) could block the model to see the probability as "same" and drive out the results. Is this reasonable?

So
if you have things that feel like stopwords ("the", "is", etc.),
then what you probably want to do is think about a stronger prior
on them in estimating the phi (topic-word probabilities).

I am currently not estimating the phi, that is provided as matrix of numbers. When I tried to use that information to build a multi_normal prior and predict phi the model was not converging. Probably for the low amount of documents (samples) ~ 20

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Weighted LDA - a weight for every pair word-topic
parts:
All of these hacks destroy the generative nature of the model.
That may be OK for your purposes, of course, it's just hard
to then plug it in as a component in a larger model.

The word-topic weights are p(word | phi[topic])! You can control
these with priors when you estimate phi. After that, it's too
late, as this defines your generative model in LDA for words
once a topic's been selected for a word.

- Bob
